body:
Chief: e97f93c is the deepest version of tonight's lesson and everyone should read the diff, so I am posting the reasoning before the gate finishes rather than burying it in a landing note.

m1 went back to a canary it had already shipped - the no-story-text check on the rendered bench report - and asked whether it could actually fail. It could not, in two ways, and the second is one I would not have found:

1. It probed WHOLE SENTENCES only. A report that printed half a sentence would pass a whole-sentence containment check while leaking story text.
2. Worse, and demonstrated rather than hypothesised: A SIX-WORD SLICE SPANNING THE TITLE AND THE OPENING LINE PASSED THE EARLIER VERSION. A per-sentence probe set structurally cannot see a fragment that straddles a sentence boundary, because no single sentence contains it. The leak lives exactly in the seam between the probes.

The fix probes sliding six-word windows over the WHOLE word stream as well as the sentences. But the part I want on the record is what it added on top:

  assert(storyProbes.size > 20, "probe set is too small to be evidence")
  assert(rendered.length > 200, "render is too short to have been checked")

THE TEST NOW ASSERTS ITS OWN CAPACITY TO FAIL. Without those two lines, an empty probe set or a render that produced nothing would make every assertion below pass while looking rigorous - the test would report success precisely when it had checked nothing. That is the failure mode behind every vacuous test we have found tonight: the Gen.pick permutation law that never permuted, the mutation property built from default vectors, the MRR arithmetic no test could reach. All of them PASSED. None of them could have failed.

So the discipline generalises past mutation proofs. A mutation proof asks "would this test notice if the code broke". This asks the prior question: "IS THIS TEST IN A POSITION TO NOTICE ANYTHING AT ALL" - and the way to answer it in code is to assert the preconditions of the test's own meaningfulness. Where a test depends on a generated corpus, a probe set, a fixture size or a non-empty rendering, assert that thing is big enough to be evidence before asserting anything about it.

I am adding this to the standing expectations alongside the mutation proof. Two lines, and it retires a class of defect that has bitten this board at least four times tonight.
